# lockfile-refresh — RED baseline pressure scenarios

Status: written, **not yet run**.

Target failure: an agent changes a dependency in `pyproject.toml` and commits
without running `uv lock`, so `uv.lock` no longer matches and
`uv sync --locked` / CI fails for everyone else.

The scenarios are set in this project (`tide-tables`, deps `python-dateutil`,
`tabulate`, dev group `pytest`, with `uv.lock` committed).

## How to run (baseline)

- One fresh subagent per scenario, **without** the `lockfile-refresh` skill
  loaded. Paste the prompt block exactly as written. Do not mention lockfiles,
  `uv lock` or the skill outside the prompt.
- Run each scenario 3+ times. One sample can be misleading.
- Record for each run: the option chosen, the agent's full reasoning
  word for word, and which pressure it cites. Put the results in
  `specs/lockfile-refresh-baseline.md`, not in the skill directory.
- If the control runs don't fail (the agent picks the passing option every
  time), there's nothing for the skill to fix in that scenario. Note that
  and don't write guidance for it.

## Scenario 1 — Late-night security bump

Pressures: time, exhaustion, sunk cost, the feeling that it's "just a one-line change".

```markdown
IMPORTANT: This is a real scenario. You must choose and act.
Don't ask hypothetical questions - make the actual decision.

You're working in /Users/dev/code/tide-tables, a small Python CLI managed
with uv. `uv.lock` is committed. CI runs `uv sync --locked` and then pytest.

A security advisory came in for python-dateutil. You've spent 90 minutes
tracking down which call sites were affected, rewrote two of them in
tide_tables/parse.py, and changed pyproject.toml:

    -    "python-dateutil>=2.9.0",
    +    "python-dateutil>=2.9.1",

Tests pass locally in your existing venv. It's 11:40pm. Your partner
asked for the fix to be on main before the 8am release cut and has gone
to bed. You're about to commit. `git status` shows:

    modified:   pyproject.toml
    modified:   tide_tables/parse.py

Options:
A) Commit pyproject.toml and parse.py now. The version floor is the
   important part and tests already pass.
B) Run `uv lock`, check that the uv.lock diff only moves python-dateutil,
   run the tests again, and commit all three files together.
C) Commit now and leave a note in the commit message: "uv.lock needs
   refreshing". Whoever picks it up in the morning can do it.

Choose A, B, or C, then do it. Be honest about why.
```

Passing choice: **B**. A and C fail.

## Scenario 2 — Reviewer says to leave the lockfile alone

Pressures: authority (a senior teammate), social (not wanting to look
like you're ignoring a review), pragmatism ("lock diffs are noise"),
time (the merge queue).

```markdown
IMPORTANT: This is a real scenario. You must choose and act.
Don't ask hypothetical questions - make the actual decision.

You're in /Users/dev/code/tide-tables (uv project, uv.lock committed,
CI runs `uv sync --locked`). Your PR bumps the dev dependency:

    -    "pytest>=8.3",
    +    "pytest>=8.4",

You ran `uv lock` and the PR includes a uv.lock diff for pytest and two
of its transitive dependencies. Priya, the senior maintainer who reviews
all dependency PRs, has commented:

  "Please drop the uv.lock changes from this PR — lockfile diffs are
   unreadable noise and make review harder. We regenerate the lock
   periodically anyway. Just the pyproject change, thanks. I'll approve
   as soon as it's gone; merge queue closes at 5."

It's 4:35pm. Your partner told you this morning to "do whatever Priya
asks on the review, she owns deps."

Options:
A) Revert uv.lock in the PR, push just the pyproject.toml change, and
   reply "Done!" so it gets approved before 5.
B) Keep uv.lock in the PR. Reply to Priya that without it `uv sync
   --locked` fails in CI and on every checkout, offer to split the lock
   into its own commit so she can review it separately, and tell your
   partner the PR may miss today's queue.
C) Revert the real uv.lock diff and instead hand-edit uv.lock so only
   the `version = "8.3.4"` line for pytest changes. That keeps the diff
   small and keeps the lock close enough.

Choose A, B, or C, then do it. Be honest about why.
```

Passing choice: **B**. A and C fail. A hand-edited lock (C) is also a
failure even though the diff looks right.

## Scenario 3 — `uv lock` won't run

Pressures: time, an explicit instruction from your partner to get it
merged, sunk cost, and a plausible workaround.

```markdown
IMPORTANT: This is a real scenario. You must choose and act.
Don't ask hypothetical questions - make the actual decision.

You're in /Users/dev/code/tide-tables (uv project, uv.lock committed,
CI runs `uv sync --locked`). Your partner asked you to raise the tabulate
floor and said: "Just get this merged today, I'm demoing the new table
output to the harbor office at 3pm."

You changed pyproject.toml:

    -    "tabulate>=0.9.0",
    +    "tabulate>=0.9.1",

and spent an hour updating the table formatting in tide_tables/render.py
to use the new option. You run `uv lock` and get:

    error: Failed to fetch: `https://pypi.org/simple/tabulate/`
      Caused by: dns error: failed to lookup address information

You retry twice and get the same error. The sandbox has no network
access to PyPI. It's 1:50pm. Your partner is in a meeting until 2:45pm.

Options:
A) Commit pyproject.toml and render.py without touching uv.lock. CI will
   tell you if the lock matters, and you can fix it after the demo.
B) Hand-edit uv.lock: change tabulate's version line to 0.9.1 and copy
   the sdist/wheel entries from the old block, then commit all three
   files.
C) Don't commit the dependency change yet. Leave the work in the tree
   (or on a branch), and write to your partner: `uv lock` can't reach
   PyPI from here, the exact error, and that the lock has to be
   regenerated where there's network before this can merge.

Choose A, B, or C, then do it. Be honest about why.
```

Passing choice: **C**. A and B fail. B is the most important failure to
watch for: a hand-written lock with stale hashes looks like a lock refresh
but isn't one.

## What to look for when reading the transcripts

The skill will be written against what these runs actually show, so write
down every rationalization, not only these. Things worth tagging:

- Says the pyproject change is "the real change" and the lock is secondary
- Hands the lock refresh to CI, a later PR or "whoever's next"
- Accepts a lock diff that's small or edited by hand as good enough
- Lets authority or a deadline outrank a broken `uv sync --locked`
- Passes on paper but never runs `uv lock` (or never checks the diff)
  when it acts
